connectionForm.advanced: Advanced: device type, port, device address
connectionForm.detectHint: “Detect automatically” works in almost all cases.
connectionForm.networkHint: The first three numbers of your IP addresses, e.g. {example}
connectionForm.noDeviceFound: No device found. Check the network or enter the address manually below.
connectionForm.portHint: Usually 502 – with a Modbus proxy, the proxy's port
connectionForm.readOnlyDevice: For this device OpenAmpere shows values; changing settings is not possible yet.
connectionForm.sameSerialHint: Two results have the same serial number: one of them is probably a Modbus proxy or data logger that passes the inverter through. Both work. Through a proxy, other programs can read at the same time.
connectionForm.searchHint: Searches your home network for inverters and detects the manufacturer and model automatically.

setup.apiKeyHint: For this you need the personal API key from the Ampere.IQ app. OpenAmpere is an independent project with no ties to EKD.
setup.cloudMayDisappear: It is unclear whether the cloud will stay available, and without it the old history can no longer be retrieved.
setup.connectsVia: To do this, OpenAmpere connects to your inverter or battery via {protocol}. Your device is detected automatically – currently supported are hybrid inverters from FoxESS (H3 series) and SAJ (H2/HS2).
setup.importIntro: Have you used your system with the “Ampere.IQ” app so far? Then you can import your history from the EKD cloud.
setup.intro: OpenAmpere shows the data of your solar system straight from your home network, without any cloud.
setup.readOnlyNotice: OpenAmpere only reads. Inverter settings are only changed once you explicitly turn on control.
setup.whatYouNeed: What you need: the IP address of the device – or we find it together.

setupHelp.cableHint: The inverter needs a connection to your home network, usually a cable in its LAN port. A cloud-only Wi-Fi stick is often not enough.
setupHelp.findIpHint: In the device list of your router (FRITZ!Box: Home Network → Network) or in the menu on the inverter's display.
setupHelp.fixedIpHint: At some point the router may give the inverter a new address. OpenAmpere then finds it again by its serial number, but a fixed address is more reliable. On a FRITZ!Box: Home Network → Network → edit device → “Always assign this network device the same IPv4 address”.
setupHelp.fixedIpTitle: Tip: assign a fixed IP address
setupHelp.modbusHint: The interface must be turned on. On the batteries sold by EKD it already is; otherwise your installer can turn it on. The usual port is 502.
setupHelp.otherManager: {lead} (e.g. the previous Smartbox) connected to the inverter? Then all connections may be in use. In that case, after setup choose “Per request” under More → Connection.
setupHelp.sajAddress: {model} (older “Ampere.StoragePro”): device address 1 or 2, depending on the communication module.
